A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same dMoE research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite expanded experiments and renumbered appendix tables.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A.4 report original 2D and 3D segmentation results and architecture ablations.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendices A.3–A.5 report original segmentation experiments, expanded external validation, additional clinical-attribute evaluations, and control-component comparisons.

M1.justification: The attribute-specific routers, shared experts, residual combination, losses, and backbone architectures remain unchanged. Section 3.2 replaces patchify/unpatchify terminology with flatten/unflatten and clarifies tensor reshaping; this documents the existing operation rather than establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds 143 radiotherapy cases from Gangnam Severance Hospital to the original Yongin cohort, introducing another external population. It also evaluates Gleason and PSA attributes as alternative clinical inputs and subgroup definitions in new Tables 9–10. The original ophthalmic and dermatological coverage remains.

E2.justification: New Table 8 compares dMoE with independently trained networks for individual attributes, and Tables 11–12 add a non-feedback control comparator. The comparator sets in the corresponding main benchmark tables remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported 3D evaluation pool increases from 132 to 275 cases, with T1 increasing from 1 to 11, and v2 explicitly reports worst-group scores. Additional comparisons introduce independent-network and non-feedback controls. Existing preprocessing, training schedules, backbones, and 2D splits remain unchanged; Table 12's retained ablation values leave their actual evaluation cohort unclear.

E4.justification: Appendix A.5 adds control-component ablations, particularly a non-feedback condition, to examine whether feedback and attribute-dependent mode switching explain performance. Feedback/MoE and dMoE comparisons already existed in the main results. The original placement and parameter-sharing ablations are retained as Tables 11–12.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without statistical uncertainty. v2 Section 4.3 introduces 95% bootstrap confidence intervals using 1,000 resamples with replacement, and Tables 1–3 display intervals for the work's aggregate and equity-scaled results. This adds substantial uncertainty reporting, without establishing additional training runs or seeds.

E6.justification: Table 3 replaces results for 132 cases with results for 275: dMoE Dice changes from 0.711 to 0.650 under different test conditions, not a demonstrated same-setting decline. Table 2 changes dMoE ES-Dice/ES-IoU from 0.841/0.749 to 0.801/0.725 while ordinary scores remain unchanged. Table 1 also revises equity scores, and new appendix comparisons add substantial results.

T1.justification: The control-system formulation, kernel approximation, linearity condition, and mode-switching derivation remain substantively unchanged. Section 3.3 expands explanations and adjusts notation, including continuous-time notation and the terminal-state index, without adding a new theorem, proof, or mathematical argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same central claims: a control-theoretic interpretation of MoE, attribute-aware dMoE, applicability to transformers and CNNs, and improved fairness in medical segmentation. Additional experiments support the existing contribution scope.

C2.justification: v2 newly connects ESSP to demographic parity and equalized odds, interprets additional clinical indicators as useful even without directly describing visible anatomy, and discusses control-component and independent-network findings. The stated limitations concerning task dependence, single-attribute modeling, and future optimization research remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract changes a promised code release to a stated available repository with an address. Section 3.2 clarifies embedding reshaping, while Table 1 newly identifies borrowed baseline scores and FairDiff equity-score recalculation. Hardware, optimizer settings, and detailed backbone architecture tables are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hardt et al. (2016) for fairness principles and the 2024 NCCN prostate-cancer guidelines for clinical-attribute motivation. The related-work section and the paper's main positioning relative to earlier MoE and fairness methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 3.3 is extensively rewritten throughout to explain layer/time correspondence, control parameters, kernel approximation, and feedback more explicitly. Section 3.2 also clarifies terminology, and the results and appendix structure gain dedicated clinical-attribute subsections. This substantially revises the central explanatory narrative despite stable mathematics.

P2.justification: Tables 1–3 are reformatted for confidence intervals, attribution notes, and worst-group markings. Figures 1 and 3 revise the stage-distribution displays, and Figure 2 updates operation labels. Three new appendix tables and expanded ablation blocks substantially extend the visual presentation; the original architecture tables are retained.

improvement.justification: The additional hospital, larger minority subgroup, bootstrap intervals, and targeted controls strengthen the empirical evidence. However, v2 introduces unresolved reporting inconsistencies: HAM10000 dMoE ES-Dice is 0.801 in Table 2 but 0.841 in Table 11, and Table 12 retains v1 ablation values under the expanded cohort counts. Its claim of consistent ES-Dice improvement also conflicts with non-feedback scoring 0.509 versus dMoE's 0.499. These problems affect central fairness evidence, preventing a reliable judgment that the benefits outweigh the loss of reporting consistency.
